description: Brahe is a modern satellite dynamics library for research and engineering, written in Rust with a Python interface, that provides coordinate transformations, perturbation models and orbit propagation for applications in space situational awareness, satellite task planning and mission operations. Its authors aim to make the algorithms easy to learn, use and verify, with a documentation site, a Rust library reference and a Journal of Open Source Software status badge. It covers Earth-orbiting satellites in general, not a fixed constellation. It is developed by Duncan Eddy with Mykel Kochenderfer, described in arXiv 2601.06452 (January 2026), and version 1.7.0 was published on PyPI on 21 July 2026. It is free under the MIT licence (copyright 2019 to 2026 Duncan Eddy), so it can be built into other tools without licence restrictions. Caveats: it is a young project and lacks the validation history of older toolkits, and high-fidelity models need user checks. It supports hazard exposure analysis and optimisation of satellite tasking and operations, such as scheduling around outages; a related record is the Orekit space flight dynamics library.
